mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for the joint signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), labor market slack reduces wage pressures and corporate cost inflation, leading to lower inflation expectations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of periods where PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below its 3-month moving average, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO < 3-month moving average, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market slowdowns (HOUST < 1800.0), reduced residential investment lowers consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where HOUST < 1800.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal a monetary policy response to rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of periods where both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase, or Rank IC for the joint signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year window.
